# `factory/executors.py`

[As built](../../README.md) › [Execution environment and infrastructure](../../subsystems/execution-environment-and-infrastructure.md) › `executors.py`

As built at `4b8570d19ee1`, read 2026-10-07.

Implements two executor protocols for running work units: DirectExecutor proves the pipeline shape with no tooling, while CommandExecutor runs a real coding harness in an isolated worktree and interrogates the resulting diff.

2,151 lines, in Execution environment and infrastructure.

## Parts

Too big to be one node, so shown in 6 parts: groups of its functions that call each other more than the rest of the file.

| Part | Lines | Functions | Largest | Calls out · in |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| **Classifying changed files as litter or real** — Walks the files touched by a run and sorts them into real changes versus litter to ignore. collect drives ignored, _classify and is_litter to decide which changed files actually count. | 432 | 9 | `collect` | 6 · 4 |
| **Running a unit and judging its outcome** — Runs a work unit end to end and classifies what came back: whether the output is a placeholder, whether there were no edits, and which tool calls were denied. unit_brief and run assemble the session route and argv, then use _is_placeholder, _no_edits_output and _denied_calls to decide what happened. | 378 | 9 | `unit_brief` | 10 · 1 |
| **Classifying changed files as litter or real** — Walks the files touched by a run and sorts them into real changes versus litter to ignore. collect drives ignored, _classify and is_litter to decide which changed files actually count. | 317 | 4 | `collect` | 6 · 4 |
| **Tracking harness spend and session outcome** — Reads and records how much a harness session spent, and derives its outcome -- success, refusal, or exhaustion -- from what the harness said. _record_session_spend, harness_spend and _session_outcome build the session_envelope and session_response that the rest of the pipeline reads. | 291 | 10 | `_record_session_spend` | 0 · 5 |
| **Invoking the harness with retries** — Launches the harness process, feeding it _task_stdin, and retries the call via _retry_if_empty when the first response comes back empty. _run_harness and _invoke are the core call, with _send_back and _retry_note handling what gets returned to the caller. | 199 | 6 | `_run_harness` | 2 · 7 |
| **Building fallback context when the harness fails** — Assembles a fallback context -- files on disk and their argv -- for use when the normal harness path can't proceed. _fallback and _fallback_context lean on files_on_disk and _context_files to reconstruct what the harness needs to see. | 174 | 5 | `_fallback` | 0 · 1 |
